commonPrompt: Read-only repository investigation. Do not modify files, access the network, or read outside this repository. You may use available search, read, directory-listing, and shell tools, including parallel calls. Answer in English, concisely. Cite full repository-relative source paths with line numbers, and name the implementation symbols supporting each requested claim. Do not rely on README claims when implementation is requested.
grading: Frozen necessary-evidence rubric: all required full relative paths appear in the final answer, one item in every symbol/behavior alternative group appears case-insensitively, at least one path:line citation is present, there is a final answer, process succeeded, and no resource cap was hit. This is reproducible evidence coverage, not a semantic proof; qualitative errors and lexical near-misses must be reported separately without changing frozen rules.

tasks.prompt: Locate how completed detail pagination and repeated file selection interact with snapshot lifetime. Explain why an original summary cursor can still select files after detail pages finish, and name the expiry/eviction authority. Cite implementation evidence, not just documentation.

Locate the cancellation path for a new content search and for continuation of an existing snapshot. Explain which layer owns the subprocess, how cancellation is observed while formatting retained evidence, and whether continuation reruns ripgrep. Cite implementation evidence.

Trace host context usage from the Pi tool adapter to the automatic choice between complete details and a summary. Identify the budget resolver and explain why explicit limits, match mode, and cursor continuation do not use a smaller adaptive budget. Cite every module in this path.
Find the definition of MAX_RESULT_BYTES. Report its exact value in bytes and cite the defining source file and line.

Locate automatic context compaction policy and execution. Explain threshold versus overflow triggering, the threshold calculation, and what happens if an extension cancels session_before_compact. Cite the responsible implementation symbols and source lines.

Locate the built-in grep output limits and user-visible truncation behavior. Explain where matching-line count, output bytes, and long-line truncation are applied, which limit a caller can increase, and the suggested way to recover full lines. Cite implementation symbols and source lines.

Trace a completed tool result from the agent loop through conversion into an OpenAI Responses function_call_output. Determine whether arbitrary tool details are serialized to the model or remain host-side metadata. Cite the result construction, message conversion, and provider serialization code.
Find the definition of DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES used by built-in tool truncation. Report its exact value in bytes and cite the defining source file and line.

Locate how directory traversal decides whether to ignore a path. Explain the precedence of explicit glob overrides versus ignore-file rules, and when hidden-file filtering is applied. Cite implementation evidence for both precedence and hidden-entry handling.

Locate the binary-detection strategies used by the searcher. Explain the difference between none, quit, and convert, including the buffered versus memory-mapped behavior, and identify where buffered input applies detection. Cite implementation symbols and source lines.

Trace --max-count from CLI parsing into the searcher and its stopping condition. Explain whether the limit counts occurrences or matching lines, whether it is per file, and how a zero value is handled. Cite the flag definition, high-level argument wiring, and search enforcement code.
Find the definition of DEFAULT_BUFFER_CAPACITY for the searcher line buffer. Report its exact value in bytes and cite the defining source file and line.
